S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.

subtypes.Fear of Weight Gain: Extreme fear and loathing of gaining weight or becoming fat.
subtypes.Fear of Specific Foods: Fear that eating high-calorie foods will immediately lead to weight gain.
subtypes.Obsession with Weight Gain: Compulsively checking the scale and becoming extremely anxious about even the slightest increase.

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.

subtypes.Distorted Body Image: Perceiving one's body as much fatter than it actually is or perceiving specific parts as excessively large when looking in the mirror.
subtypes.Self-Worth Dependent on Weight: Judging whether one is a good or successful person solely based on weight or body shape.

S047.name: Compensatory_Behavior_NonPurging
S047.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors to prevent weight gain without purging (direct removal of food).

subtypes.Fasting: Intentionally stopping food intake for a certain period to prevent weight gain.
subtypes.Excessive Exercise: Repetitively performing exercise at a level that exceeds physical limits to prevent weight gain.

S048.name: Compensatory_Behavior_Purging
S048.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors involving the expulsion of food or fluids to prevent weight gain.

subtypes.Self-Induced Vomiting: Intentionally inducing vomiting to remove ingested food.
subtypes.Misuse of Medications: Repetitively misusing laxatives, diuretics, or enemas for the purpose of weight control.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

patient_info.stressor_event: Gaining a new family member (e.g., birth, adoption, older adult moving in)
patient_info.stressor: Ace and his spouse took in an older relative from Taiwan for an extended stay, and the household quickly centered on shared meals, family harmony, and careful attention to whether everyone was eating enough. Over the following 6 months, Ace’s usually relaxed cooking life became more charged: after tense family dinners or late cashier shifts, he began having discrete episodes of eating much more than planned with a sense that he could not stop, then tried to compensate through both purging and nonpurging methods. He became increasingly fearful of weight gain and let weight and shape influence how he judged himself, despite the pattern not yet causing major work disruption. Ace brought it up himself during a routine visit with his primary-care clinician, who referred him for psychiatric assessment before the cycle became more entrenched.

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.
S045.manifestation: If the scale is even a pound higher in the morning, I get this panicky feeling that I’m sliding into being fat, and I start avoiding rice or anything oily at family meals even when I know one meal shouldn’t matter that much.

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.
S046.manifestation: When my cashier shirt pulls a little at my stomach, I spend the whole shift feeling like customers can tell I have no discipline, and my mood about myself depends way too much on how I look that day.

S047.name: Compensatory_Behavior_NonPurging
S047.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors to prevent weight gain without purging (direct removal of food).
S047.manifestation: After a night when I eat too much, I’ll often skip breakfast and lunch or make myself walk for a long time before work, not because I enjoy it but because I feel like I have to cancel out what I did.

S048.name: Compensatory_Behavior_Purging
S048.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors involving the expulsion of food or fluids to prevent weight gain.
S048.manifestation: There have been times after everyone goes to bed when I make myself throw up in the bathroom or take laxatives, telling myself it’s just to undo the damage, even though afterward I feel embarrassed and shaky.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: On bad nights I can eat a full plate of leftovers, then keep going through bread, snacks, and ice cream in the kitchen within an hour or two, way more than I’d ever eat if someone were sitting with me.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: What brought me in is that some nights after work or a tense dinner, I start eating and it feels like the decision-making part of me shuts off, like I can see myself reaching for more food but I can’t make myself stop.

additional_requirement_1.name: Additional Requirement 1
additional_requirement_1.description: The binge eating and inappropriate compensatory behaviors both occur, on average, at least once a week for 3 months
additional_requirement_1.manifestation: For the last few months, it’s been happening most weeks that I have one of those out-of-control eating nights, and then I try to make up for it by throwing up, taking laxatives, skipping meals, or forcing a long walk.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: I’m still showing up for my cashier shifts and handling my responsibilities, but I’ve started avoiding some family meals afterward or acting distracted because I’m worried about what I ate or what I’ll do to compensate.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This has been going on for about 6 months, since our older relative came to stay with us and meals at home became more stressful for me.
